content: HEY2, also referred to as cardiovascular helix-loop-helix factor 1 (CHF1), is a protein encoded by the HEY2 gene in humans. CHF1 belongs to the hairy and enhancer of split-related (HESR) family of basic helix-loop-helix (bHLH) transcription factors. The protein encoded by this gene can form either homodimers or heterodimers, which localize to the nucleus. Within the nucleus, these dimers interact with a histone deacetylase complex to repress transcriptional activity. The expression of the HEY2 gene is regulated by the Notch signaling pathway. In mice, two similar and functionally redundant genes are essential for embryonic cardiovascular development. These genes are also implicated in neurogenesis and somitogenesis. Additionally, alternatively spliced transcript variants of HEY2 have been identified, but their biological significance remains undetermined. From a clinical perspective, common genetic variants in HEY2, as well as in SCN5A and SCN10A, have been associated with Brugada syndrome, a cardiac arrhythmia disorder. HEY2 has been demonstrated to interact with Sirtuin 1 (SIRT1) and Nuclear receptor co-repressor 1 (NCOR1), suggesting its involvement in complex regulatory pathways.
